children: shares dropped about 1% in premarket trading Friday after Bank of America cut its rating and price target, citing a recovery that may take longer as weak demand in key parts of the business weighs on the outlook.

BofA lowered its target to $30 from $47 and reduced its fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings-per-share forecasts to $1.43 and $1.87. The brokerage now expects Nike's sales to remain under pressure through fiscal 2027, delaying a broader rebound.

China remains an additional challenge. Nike's revenue in Greater China declined 17% in the latest quarter, while changes to its e-commerce distribution strategy could create further pressure on sales in the near term.
BofA also pointed to weaker consumer purchases of established footwear styles and caution among retailers. It said future earnings could depend more on improving gross margins and reducing expenses.

Nike reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $46.4 billion, little changed from the prior year, while net income fell 3% to $3.1 billion. BofA's fiscal 2027 forecast also implies a 107% dividend payout ratio.

title: BofA Turns Bearish on Nike Stock, Sees More Pressure Ahead
